items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: Then he would play -- tape it off with Victor Herbert -- you know what I mean -- his songs.

ctx.x: That was quite a milestone for a black man at that time.

Oh, yes, sir. And in that city he knew all of the millionaires, all of the big oil people. They were all crazy about Gordon C. Harrison. And Gordon C. Harrison, what he would do, between numbers he would play the classics. He played the beautiful classics. Then he would play -- tape it off with Victor Herbert -- you know what I mean -- his songs. Like "Kiss Me Again" and those type of songs, you know what I mean. And he played so beautifully. And the people would just sit at the table and just "Oh" -- you know…

Well, this was the man that really broke me in, and that taught me the mannerisms -- you know what I mean -- of -- or the dynamics of music, and how you should tone your music down -- you know what I mean. In other words, you play according to the occasions. And I never forgot it.
